chapter: New Orleans style and bass playing
title: Ensemble playing in the Ory band versus Armstrong's solos
summary: Turetsky asks whether Armstrong led away from ensemble; Garland says Louis was unpredictable and traded phrases with the clarinet.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Sometimes many writers talk about Louis Armstrong leading away from playing as an ensemble into solo playing more and many of them say that Louie was, perhaps, one of the first great soloists. And I just wondered if the band playing -- like the Ory band, when you were with Ory, you played a lot of ensemble things --
-- in other words everybody seemed to be playing more, Pappa Mutt might come out front for a little bit, but Ory and Joe were playing still in the band --
As opposed to Louie, just playing a solo with the rhythm section, is that -- did Louie change that, is that true what the books say, or did we always have solo?

No I don't -- no, Louie -- Louie had a lot of stuff of his own, you understand? Louie -- one thing about Louie, you don't know what Louie's going to do half the time, you understand? Louie get out there and take one by himself, you understand, he might take few bars, you understand and then go along and bar over to the clarinet and the clarinet pick up where he left off at, you know?
